questions.questionHtml:
🔥 GATE 2027 Original: Operating Systems - Deadlocks

A system has 3 processes $P_1, P_2, P_3$ and 12 units of a single resource type $R$. Current allocations and maximum demands are:
• $P_1$: Allocated = 3, Max = 8
• $P_2$: Allocated = 2, Max = 5
• $P_3$: Allocated = 4, Max = 9
If process $P_2$ requests 1 additional unit of $R$, can the request be safely granted?

💡 Detailed Concept & Solution:
Total resources = 12. Total allocated currently = $3 + 2 + 4 = 9$. Available = $12 - 9 = 3$.
If $P_2$ is granted 1 unit: $P_2$ allocation becomes 3, Available becomes $3 - 1 = 2$.
Remaining needs:
Need($P_1$) = $8 - 3 = 5$
Need($P_2$) = $5 - 3 = 2$
Need($P_3$) = $9 - 4 = 5$
With Available = 2, Need($P_2$) $\le 2$ can be satisfied! $P_2$ finishes and releases all 3 units, making Available = $2 + 3 = 5$.
Now Need($P_1$) = 5 or Need($P_3$) = 5 can both be satisfied sequentially. Hence $\langle P_2, P_1, P_3 \rangle$ is a valid safe sequence.

A read-after-write(RAW) data dependency occurs when a later instruction requires an input value that is set by an earlier instruction. A RAW data hazard occurs when one instruction writes a value into a register that will be used as input by a later instruction, but that value does not actually appear in the register by the cycle on which the later instruction attempts to read it.
Note that a RAW data hazard always implies a RAW data dependency, but some RAW data dependencies do not imply a RAW data hazard.

Here is a definition for a set of trees called GO trees.
Basis: A single vertex with no edges is a GO tree. The root is the only vertex in the tree.

Recursive rule: If T1T1 and T2T2 are GO trees, then a new GO tree TT' can be constructed by first placing T1T1 to the left of T2T2 , adding a new vertex v at the top and then adding an edge between vv and the root of T1T1 and an edge between vv and the root of T2T2 . The new vertex v is the root of T′T′.


Exclusion statement: TT is a GO tree only if TT is the tree described in the Basis or TT can be constructed by repeatedly applying the recursive rule starting with the tree given in the basis.
Which of the following trees is/are NOT a GO tree?

  1. struct node {
  2.     int value;
  3.     struct node *next;
  4. };
  5. typedef struct node Node;
  6.

  8.     if(head== NULL) return 1;
  9.     Node *p,*q;
  10.     p = head;

  12.     while(q!=NULL && q!=p){
  13.         q = q->next;
  14.     if(q==NULL) return 1;
  15.     q = q->next;
  16.     p = p->next;
  17.     }
  18. return (q==NULL);
